survivors_flagged.one_line: The Anglo American merger has cleared everywhere except China's SAMR, which reportedly wants copper-supply commitments. Anglo still guides to closing by March 2027. This is a stock-for-stock spread trade with China timing risk, not a fresh early-arc setup.

Activist Irenic is pushing for a sale. The OEM sale closed in August ($1.5B net). The $530M Acute Care/Urology sale to Intersurgical is due to close in Q4-26. The company plans a $1B buyback and has a new CEO and chair. The stock barely moved (~$123-127), but sale-of-company risk remains unconfirmed.

Blackstone $61.25 cash deal: PUCT/FERC/NRC/HSR done; on 2026-10-16 the New Mexico regulator (NMPRC) accepted the amended application; hearings set for Jan 19-Feb 1 2027; outside date 2027-05-31; close expected 1H27. A dated regulatory arb, but long-dated and widely tracked.

verified.catalyst: China's SAMR clearance of the Anglo American-Teck all-stock merger (1.3301 Anglo shares per Teck share). SAMR is reportedly negotiating copper-concentrate supply assurances, and South Korea is also reportedly still pending.
verified.dated_milestone: Closing is guided within the Sept-2026 to Mar-2027 window (mlex, Oct-2026). Next date: a SAMR remedy decision, expected by end-Q1 2027, with no fixed date announced.
verified.instrument: TECK common (NYSE). The spread would need to be hedged by shorting 1.3301 Anglo shares (AAL.L, or NGLOY ADRs at 0.5 share each) per Teck share.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 passes: a named counterparty (Anglo American) and a named regulator (SAMR). G2 passes: a signed definitive merger agreement at a fixed 1.3301 exchange ratio. G3 fails: the spread is already closed once the Anglo special dividend is netted out, so no currently unpriced figure is left.
verified.edge: L. Before the deal was announced (around 2025-09-08), Teck traded near US$34. At $62.95 today, the run-up is about +85%, much of it copper beta. The remaining capture is about 0%. On 2026-11-02, NGLOY $25.71 x 2 gives $51.42 per Anglo share. Netting out the roughly $4.19 per share special dividend that goes only to pre-merger Anglo holders leaves $47.23. Multiplied by 1.3301, that implies $62.82 per Teck share, against Teck at $62.95, so the spread is about -0.2%. The trade is fully harvested, and the holder keeps China timing and break risk with no premium for it.
verified.primary_source: mlex, "Anglo American still sees Teck Resources deal completing by March" (Oct-2026). reporteminero.cl on SAMR's copper-supply demand (2026-10). Teck Form 6-K / merger circular on SEC EDGAR, giving the 1.3301 ratio and the $4.5B (~$4.19/sh) special dividend (2025). FMP batch quotes for TECK $62.945, NGLOY $25.71 and AAL.L 3824p (2026-11-02).
verified.analysis: The event is real, dated and still ahead, but the stock-for-stock deal leaves no residual spread. Netting out the $4.5B (about $4.19 per share) special dividend, which goes only to Anglo holders, Teck already trades at or slightly above deal-implied value. The upside comes from the contractual ratio, not from a derived valuation, so the numerator-provenance check does not apply. What remains is the SAMR copper-supply remedy timing (reportedly no asset sales demanded) and a small break risk, uncompensated, plus outright copper exposure if unhedged. That is a macro and commodity bet, not an event edge. Gap: the GBP/ADR cross was taken from NGLOY rather than a live AAL.L x GBPUSD fix, and the special-dividend per-share figure is "subject to adjustment", so the spread estimate carries about ±1pp error. That is not enough to change the verdict.

verified.catalyst: CVC and GTCR made a joint take-private approach (reported 2026-04-22, still unconfirmed and without a price). It sits on top of Irenic's sale campaign, the $1.0B buyback funded by about $1.8B of divestiture proceeds, and the pending close of the Acute Care/Urology sale to Intersurgical.
verified.dated_milestone: Q3-26 results call on 2026-11-05 (status of the bid and buyback, plus Intersurgical close timing). Next date is the Acute Care/Urology close, guided for Q4-26.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 partial: counterparties CVC/GTCR are named but only as a reported, unconfirmed approach with no price. G2 yes: the $1.0B buyback and $800M debt paydown are company-committed, though their execution pace is undisclosed. G3 no: there is no specific unpriced figure, because the bid price was never disclosed.
verified.edge: L. (a) Run-up: from $124.75 (the 2026-04-21 close before the bid report) to $140.89 today is +12.9%. The stock is near its 52-week high of $145 and above its 50-day ($131) and 200-day ($125) averages. So the triage figure of ~$123-127 is stale and the bid premium is largely back in the price. (b) Remaining: there is no disclosed offer price to measure against. The one roundup that called the deal "agreed" put EV at ~$5.5B, roughly today's $5.97B market cap, which would imply about 0% left. A typical 20-30% take-private premium on the pre-bid base would mean about $150-162, or 7-15% left. The cost of being wrong is about -12% back to the ~$125 base if the approach is dead.
verified.primary_source: Bloomberg via news.bgov.com, "CVC and GTCR Said to Make Take-Private Offer for Teleflex" (2026-04-22). Teleflex 8-K Ex 99.1 responding to Irenic (2026-03-27). Business Wire Q3-26 call notice (2026-10-22, call 2026-11-05). FMP quote TFX $140.89 (2026-11-02).
verified.analysis: The CVC/GTCR approach (Bloomberg/Reuters, 2026-04-22) is real but six months old. It has no confirmed price or agreement, and FMP news from 2026-09-15 to 2026-11-02 has no follow-up, only R&D and earnings-call notices. Meanwhile the stock has rerated to $140.89, about +13% above the pre-bid base, so most of a plausible sale premium already looks priced. I did not do the 10-Q waterfall check (the lookup budget went to bid status). The divestiture proceeds are earmarked $1.0B buyback / $0.8B debt, with no preferred ahead of the common, but there is no SoP figure to re-derive. So the score is on the EQUITY's remaining capture, capped at 4. The 2026-11-05 Q3 call is the near-term test: confirmation of a process or a signed deal would upgrade it, and silence leaves a ~12% downside back to the base.

verified.catalyst: Blackstone Infrastructure's $61.25/sh cash takeout of TXNM needs only one more approval, from the NMPRC. The commission accepted the amended application on 2026-10-16, with $220M of rate credits and other customer benefits; evidentiary hearings run Jan 19 to Feb 1 2027 and the deal must close by the 2027-05-31 outside date.
verified.dated_milestone: NMPRC evidentiary hearings 2027-01-19 to 2027-02-01, then a hearing-examiner recommended decision and a commission vote. Merger outside date 2027-05-31; company guides to a 1H27 close. NMPRC has no statutory deadline for the revised application.
verified.instrument: TXNM common (NYSE), merger-arb long at about $58.50
verified.bloom_gates: G1 (named acquirer: Blackstone Infrastructure) + G2 (signed merger agreement at $61.25 cash, outside date 2027-05-31, a $175M reverse termination fee after TXNM waived half of the original $350M). G3 is not met: the $2.75 spread is visible and widely tracked, so nothing about the price is unpriced.
verified.edge: L. The spread is only fair pay for a real regulatory binary. RUN-UP: about +22% from the roughly $48 pre-rumor/pre-announcement base (spring 2025) to $58.50 today, so about 78% of the deal value is already harvested. REMAINING: +4.7% gross to $61.25, or about +6% including about 2 quarterly dividends (assumed permitted), which is about 10% annualized over 7 months. The market implies about 75-80% odds of approval. The NMPRC is hostile: it rejected Avangrid-PNM in 2021, voted 2-1 to void the $400M Blackstone stock sale, and opponents are contesting the fee waiver. A break back to about $47-48 standalone is roughly -18%, against +5-6% if the deal closes. That is consensus arb pricing with no informational edge.
verified.primary_source: TXNM 10-Q for Q3-2026 (sec.gov pnm-20260930.htm, filed ~2026-10-30); TXNM 8-K dated 2026-10-27 (hearing schedule Jan 19-Feb 1 2027); FMP quote 2026-11-02 ($58.495); SourceNM 2026-08-04 (opposition over the fee waiver)
verified.analysis: The catalyst is real, dated and still ahead: NMPRC is the sole remaining approval (FERC Feb-2026, PUCT settlement, NRC 2026-08-21), and hearings are set for Jan 19 to Feb 1 2027. But it is mostly harvested. The stock has moved from about $48 to $58.50 and only about 4.7% gross is left to the $61.25 cash price. The downside is asymmetric (about -18% on a break) given this commission's 2021 Avangrid rejection, its 2-1 vote to void the stock sale, and TXNM halving the reverse break fee to $175M, which weakens the cushion if the deal fails. Capped at 4 under the residual-capture rule. The deal price is contractual cash, so the numerator-provenance rule does not apply. Gaps: the pre-catalyst base of about $48 is from memory, not re-pulled, and dividend permissibility was not re-checked.
